newsitem.title: PERU: Peru oil contract auctions draw four foreign firms.
newsitem.headline: Peru oil contract auctions draw four foreign firms.

text.p: The government's auction of two licences to explore and exploit oil blocks in the north of Peru has drawn bids from Canadian, Italian, Argentine and U.S. firms, an energy and mines ministry source said.
The United States' Occidental Petroleum Corp, Argentina's Perez Companc and a consortium of Canada's Ranger Oil and Italy's Agip SpA bid to explore the 274,000-hectare block, Z-1, the source said.
For the auction of the 348,000-hectare block, Z-3, the Italian-Canadian group was the only bidder, he added.
The winning bids, to be announced May 2, will go to the firm offering to pay the highest royalty tax payments on oil produced from the blocks.
The blocks are in the coastal department of Piura about 650 miles (1,050 km) north of Lima, according to state oil licensing agent Perupetro. Details of the blocks' reserves were not available.
Since Perupetro started offering licenses four years ago, 15 have started producing oil, while 22 are at the exploration stage.

Perupetro is negotiating five more exploration and development contracts with U.S. companies Coastal and Atlantic Richfield Company ; Argentina's Pluspetrol; Britain's Enterprise Oil, and Peru's Buenaventura Ingenieros, according to the Energy and Mines ministry.
